chunks: From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning the female apostate from Islam, he said:

"She is not to be killed; rather, she is to be put to hard service, and food and drink are withheld from her except what sustains her life, and she is to be clothed in coarse garments, and she is to be beaten regarding the prayers."

key_terms.خَشِنَ ٱلثِّيَابِ: coarse garments; rough clothing imposed upon her
key_terms.خِدْمَةً شَدِيدَةً: hard service; severe labor imposed as punishment
key_terms.لَا تُقْتَلُ: she is not to be killed; the stated legal penalty is not execution
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَوَاتِ: the prayers; salat (prayer), in relation to which disciplinary force is mentioned
key_terms.ٱلطَّعَامَ وَٱلشَّرَابَ: food and drink; sustenance restricted except for survival
key_terms.ٱلْإِسْلَامِ: Islam; the religion from which apostasy is being described
key_terms.ٱلْمُرْتَدَّةِ: the female apostate; a woman who has turned back from Islam

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhib al-Ahkam say about the ruling on a female apostate in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning the female apostate from Islam. It states that she is not to be executed, and instead describes punitive and coercive measures applied to her, including hard service, restricted sustenance, coarse clothing, and disciplinary beating concerning salat (prayer).
